Sahil (AE): ACME sent back a redline overnight. They changed Price Protection to an open MFN for 12 months and want it to apply to any future promotional pricing.
Lina (PS): Yikes. That would block our seasonal promos and any pilot discounts we give to other prospects.
Jordan (Legal): Clause they added: "For the term, Customer shall receive the lowest price Redwood offers to any customer for substantially similar services." No exclusions; it's broad.
Tom (Pricing Ops): Practically speaking that language could require retroactive credits if we run a later promo. We need either carveouts or a firm monetary cap.
Sahil (AE): They also asked to make the POC 50% off first 2 months. If that becomes the "lowest price" we're stuck.
Jordan (Legal): I'm proposing a three-part approach: (1) carveouts that exclude time-limited promos and channel/partner pricing, (2) a explicit non-precedent clause for one-off concessions (POCs), and (3) a dollar cap on retroactive credits.
Nora (CFO): What's a defensible cap? We want to limit balance-sheet exposure but also be reasonable for negotiations.
Tom (Pricing Ops): Suggest cap = min(3 months of invoiced fees for the customer, $200k). That limits large enterprise exposure while giving small customers a practical cushion.
Lina (PS): Can we tie the cap to a minimum post-POC commit? Like cap applies only if customer executes a committed ARR >= $150k; otherwise we keep a stricter reversion clause.
Jordan (Legal): Good idea. Draft language sample: 
```
Notwithstanding any MFN or price-protection provision, the parties agree that (a) one-time concessions identified in Schedule X (including POC concessions) are non-recurring and are excluded from MFN comparisons; (b) time-limited promotional offers of thirty (30) days or less, and channel/partner or reseller programs, are excluded from MFN; and (c) Redwood's aggregate liability for any retroactive price adjustments resulting from an MFN determination shall not exceed the lesser of (i) three (3) months of fees actually paid by Customer and (ii) $200,000.
```
Sahil (AE): If we add the commit condition on Lina's suggestion, we can offer POC discount with safe guards. ACME might push on the $200k cap.
Tom (Pricing Ops): We could make the cap tiered: $50k for <100k ARR commit, $200k for >=150k commit. Keeps it flexible.
Nora (CFO): I'm comfortable with tiered cap tied to minimum committed ARR. Approve the POC concession (50% x 2 months) subject to legal carveouts and tiered cap.
DealDeskBot: Deal Desk ticket DD-4998 opened by Sahil (AE): ACME POC concession + MFN redline review. Status: Pending pricing approval.
Jordan (Legal): I'll send a redline back with the carveouts + tiered cap language and the non-precedent clause. Recommend we mark promo <30 days and partner/channel explicitly.
Lina (PS): Also add an explicit line that MFN covers pricing for "substantially similar services" and not feature parity or roadmap commitments. Buyers sometimes weaponize MFN to demand features.
Sahil (AE): Noted. I'll attach the POC SOW and the minimum ARR commitment language to the Deal Desk ticket.
Tom (Pricing Ops): Once Jordan posts the redline, I'll update the rate card notes and record the concession in the pricing system so it doesn't get re-used accidentally.
Sahil (AE): Thanks team — plan: send redline, attach POC SOW, ask ACME to accept carveouts or counter with less broad language. Will follow up after their reply.
Nora (CFO): Approve contingent on the carveouts + tiered cap. If ACME refuses carveouts, we walk.
Jordan (Legal): On it. ETA ~3 hours.
DealDeskBot: DD-4998 updated: Legal redline uploaded.
Lina (PS): Great. :thumbsup:
